title: Ollantaytambo
summary: Ollantaytambo, in Peru's Cusco region, was a royal estate of the Inka Empire with a palace and temple complex at the meeting of the Patacancha and Urubamba rivers. Peru's tourism board describes it as a military, religious and agricultural centre built when the empire was expanding most, and as the scene of a battle between Manco Inca and Spanish troops in 1536.

uncertainty.note: The range is the Inka period as defined in the Antiquity article (c. AD 1400-1532). No opened page gives a construction year; peru.travel says only that construction dates to the Inka Empire's period of greatest expansion, linked to Pachacutec's reign.
